findings.detail: 'op' is allocated via the non-zeroing PyObject_GC_New() and freed with Py_DECREF(op) at line 262 while op->ob_item still hold allocator garbage — those members are written only *after* the free (or only on a branch that does not dominate it), and the file's destructor decrefs/visits them (see line 567). tp_dealloc/tp_clear then acts on an uninitialized value (crash, dominant under OOM). Fix: NULL/initialize these members immediately after the allocation, before the first fallible call.

'di' is allocated via the non-zeroing PyObject_GC_New() and freed with Py_DECREF(di) at line 1952 while di->di_current, di->di_odict, di->kind still hold allocator garbage — those members are written only *after* the free (or only on a branch that does not dominate it), and the file's destructor decrefs/visits them (see line 1719). tp_dealloc/tp_clear then acts on an uninitialized value (crash, dominant under OOM). Fix: NULL/initialize these members immediately after the allocation, before the first fallible call.

zeroing_by_evidence.PyType_GenericAlloc: forwards to _PyType_AllocNoTrack, which memsets the object after the PyObject header (Objects/typeobject.c:2542)

allocator_model.tp_alloc_rule: a `->tp_alloc(...)` call counts as non-zeroing only in a file that registers its own allocfunc returning raw storage; the two in-tree instances are Modules/_datetimemodule.c time_alloc / datetime_alloc
